lessons: Build one AdmissionHold per journal in _SharedControl and pass it into compose_pipeline/compose_merge_queue. Do not construct a new hold per dispatch: Runner.dispatch calls the pipeline factory once per ticket, so an in-memory red set never reaches K=3.

Alternatively, rebuild the red streak from journaled integration outcomes when the hold is constructed, so the streak, green reset, and fresh-streak-after-release rule survive across dispatches and restarts.
Add a test that drives three distinct integration reds through three separate production factory calls (or three compose_pipeline calls on one journal) and asserts the hold fires.

DispatchPause seeds hold_id from next(iter(inbox.holds)), so after a restart it adopts a rehydrated admission hold. Seed the pause only from pause-owned holds, and never let a pause discard_hold an admission hold id.
Add a restart test: with an admission hold active, rebuild the control factory, assert allow_offer() is true, and assert a matching resume still releases the admission hold.

Check whether the dispatch-pause fix needs an edit to squatch/daemon.py, which is outside the fence. If it does, the ticket's reject condition applies; prefer a fix in __main__.py, e.g. clear the pause's adopted id when it belongs to the admission hold.
In eval/shakeout/bench.py, build the inbox once per journal, not inside the per-dispatch factory. Each compose_daemon_control call appends a control_lifecycle signal.
reason: Checks passed; the review found two concrete, fixable wiring defects (a per-dispatch hold rebuild and pause adopting the admission hold), each with a clear paved road.
